objective: Define the provider-neutral handoff contract that allows later telephony, messaging, calendar, automation, and AMS adapters to reference canonical River CRM insurance relationships without selecting a provider, creating a second identity system, introducing transport behavior, or changing the existing River CRM schema.

architecture.canonicalIdentity: RiverCrmRelationshipId remains the only canonical relationship identity passed across the insurance integration boundary.
architecture.canonicalEvents: RiverCrmRelationshipEvent remains the canonical lifecycle/event record. Provider identifiers may appear only as optional external references.
architecture.providerNeutrality: INS-001E defines provider-neutral request/context contracts only. No Twilio, RingCentral, OpenPhone, carrier, AMS, calendar, email, or other provider implementation is selected or imported.
architecture.transportBoundary: No HTTP webhook, outbound API request, phone call, SMS, email, dialer, bridge, recording, or carrier request is executed by INS-001E.
architecture.persistenceBoundary: No new D1 migration or provider-specific persistence table is required. Existing relationship, acquisition, consent, insurance profile, and event records remain authoritative.
architecture.handoffTarget: INS-002 may consume these contracts to implement Instant Contact / Call Orchestration without restructuring INS-001 canonical records.

providerNeutralExternalReference.rule: Provider-specific identifiers never replace RiverCrmRelationshipId, eventId, consentId, or any other canonical River identifier.
providerNeutralExternalReference.canonicalStorage: When a provider-originated lifecycle event is later persisted, its provider identifier may be represented through RiverCrmRelationshipEvent.externalReference.
requirements: External references must be normalized non-empty text when supplied.
An external reference must never be treated as a relationship identifier.
INS-001E does not create provider-specific ID brands because no provider has been selected.
No provider credentials, API keys, phone-number SIDs, call SIDs, message SIDs, or carrier identifiers are introduced.

integrationContext.name: InsuranceGrowthIntegrationContext
integrationContext.purpose: Provide later adapters with the minimum canonical context needed to make an independently governed integration decision without rereading or restructuring the River CRM domain.
rules: relationshipId is required and canonical.
Insurance profile fields originate from InsuranceLeadProfile or InsuranceLeadPresentation.
Acquisition context remains optional.
Contact channels preserve canonical channel and consent status semantics.
doNotContact must remain explicit and may never be silently overridden.
The context does not contain provider credentials or transport-specific configuration.
The context does not duplicate generic CRM display name, owner, stage, follow-up, or appointment state.

contactEligibility.purpose: Expose facts needed by later orchestration without making INS-001E itself a dialer or messaging engine.
rules: A channel with granted consent may be represented as available context.
Denied, revoked, unknown, or missing consent is never converted into granted consent.
doNotContact true is preserved as suppression context.
INS-001E does not decide legal compliance beyond preserving the canonical consent and suppression facts already stored by INS-001.
INS-001E does not send or schedule contact.
The resulting event must use the canonical RiverCrmRelationshipEvent constructor.
The event type is always callback-requested.
relationshipId remains canonical River CRM identity.
Provider-specific identifiers may appear only as optional externalReference.
Optional callback details are stored only in canonical event metadata.
The builder performs no persistence.
The builder performs no phone call, SMS, email, scheduling, or provider request.
Notes are bounded plain text and must not contain arbitrary nested provider payloads.

handoffContract.name: InsuranceGrowthIntegrationHandoff
handoffContract.purpose: Represent the stable data package INS-002 or another separately governed adapter may consume.
rules: context is provider-neutral InsuranceGrowthIntegrationContext.
triggerEvent is a canonical RiverCrmRelationshipEvent.
Both records must reference the same relationshipId.
The handoff is immutable data only.
Creating a handoff does not mean the contact attempt is authorized, scheduled, sent, dialed, or completed.
Adapters remain responsible for provider-specific authentication, idempotency, retries, transport, webhook verification, and delivery/call lifecycle handling.

validation: Reject mismatched relationship identities between context and trigger event.
Reject malformed callback requested channel values.
Reject empty or whitespace-only provider external references.
Preserve optional acquisition context without inventing source or campaign.
Never convert provider identifiers into canonical River IDs.
tests: Build provider-neutral integration context from canonical insurance presentation data.
Preserve product interest, quote status, state, and postal code.
Preserve optional acquisition source and campaign.
Preserve canonical contact channel consent statuses.
Do not duplicate generic CRM display name, owner, stage, follow-up, or appointment fields.
Allow optional provider externalReference without changing canonical identity.
Place bounded callback details only in canonical event metadata.
Build provider-neutral handoff from matching context and trigger event.
Contain no telephony, SMS, email, dialer, bridge, recording, calendar, carrier, or AMS runtime.
Contain no Sesh source or runtime dependency.
acceptanceCriteria: River CRM relationship identity remains canonical across the integration boundary.
Provider identifiers remain optional external references only.
A provider-neutral insurance integration context can be created from existing canonical insurance presentation data.
Canonical consent and do-not-contact facts survive the handoff unchanged.
A callback-requested event can be created without persistence or transport behavior.
The callback event uses the existing canonical RiverCrmRelationshipEvent contract.
A provider-neutral handoff can bind context to a matching canonical trigger event.
No provider SDK, credential, webhook route, network transport, telephony runtime, messaging runtime, or AMS runtime is introduced.
Repository-wide existing type debt is not broadened into INS-001E.
Working-tree scope remains limited to the four planned INS-001E files.

readyWhen: INS-002 can receive canonical relationship identity without inventing provider identity.
INS-002 can evaluate preserved consent and suppression context before provider transport.
INS-002 can create or consume callback-requested canonical lifecycle events.
INS-002 can attach provider event/call/message identifiers as external references without schema redesign.
Provider selection and transport behavior remain independently governable.
